title: Lyons-Peres Question 17.18 (our id P0033): REFUTED - a Galton-Watson-stationary AND/OR colour flow is non-ergodic under equivalence
body:
Lyons and Peres, Probability on Trees and Networks (version 19 August 2026), Question 17.18 (p. 575) asks whether a consistent equivariant flow rule admitting a stationary measure EQUIVALENT to Galton-Watson measure must induce an ergodic Markov chain; their Proposition 17.17 proves it when all child weights are strictly positive, and Exercise 17.22 gives a non-ergodic example whose stationary measure is only absolutely continuous, so equivalence is the point of the question. Our result (id P0033, 2026-09-08): NO. Take Galton-Watson with P(D=2) = 3/5, P(D=3) = 2/5 (mean 12/5) and an isomorphism-invariant colour in {0,1} defined by AND at two-child vertices and OR at three-child vertices; both preserve unanimity, so every vertex has at least one child of its own colour, and the flow chooses uniformly among those. Galton-Watson measure is stationary, the root colour is invariant along the chain and takes each value with probability 1/2 - a non-constant invariant function, hence no ergodicity - and the stationary measure equals Galton-Watson measure, trivially equivalent to it. The colour exists because F(p) = (3/5) p^2 + (2/5)[1 - (1-p)^3] fixes 1/2, and r_n = E[q_n^2] satisfies r_{n+1} = 3/10 + (3/5) r^2 + (2/5) r^3 whose increment factors as (r - 1/2)[(2/5) r^2 + (4/5) r - 3/5], driving r_n from r_0 = 1/4 up to 1/2 and giving E[q(1-q)] = 0. Verification as the source words it: the step the proof leaves implicit, and which was checked, is that Galton-Watson really is stationary - it holds because, conditioned on the children's colours, the child subtrees are independent, each distributed as Galton-Watson conditioned on its own colour, so the chosen subtree is exactly GW given colour = c, the uniform choice adds no bias, and mixing over c returns GW. Prior art unchecked; the tree-automaton and factor-of-iid literature is where to look.
Galton-Watson with P(D=2) = 3/5, P(D=3) = 2/5
consistent equivariant flow rule choosing uniformly among same-coloured children

title: Open problem: Endogeny of nonminimal discounted-tree fixed points
body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status candidate_partial_counterexample). Determine whether every positive-index invariant RTP from Corollary33 and condition39 is nonendogenous. Source: Aldous and Bandyopadhyay: A survey of max-type recursive distributional equations, Conjecture34;PDF26-30. Status notes: Bounded primary-source and focused later-literature search on2026-09-07; later geometric endogeny and discounted boundedness advances credited. No full current-openness certificate.

title: Attempt on Endogeny of nonminimal discounted-tree fixed points
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact recurrence, conditional-law calculation, or source-specific limiting obstruction Result: Set N=2, eta=0, xi1=xi2=1 and Y=1 deterministically. Every ray sum is0, the homogeneous equation fixes Y, condition39 holds, and every iterate from aY has law delta_a. The all-a tree process is invariant and endogenous because its root is constant. Thus the literal conjecture needs an additional assumption. Check: The conditional root law is delta_a and its only self-coupling is diagonal, independently confirming endogeny. Positive constant marks would make the ray sum infinite; strict constant discounts would destroy the chosen positive homogeneous fixed point. Obstruction: This is a degenerate scope correction, not a solution of the substantive nondegenerate version or a novelty claim.

title: Open problem: ISE scaling limit of critical high-dimensional percolation clusters of fixed size
body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For critical percolation on Z^d, d > 6, show that the empirical measure of the cluster of the origin, rescaled by n^{-1/4} in space, conditioned on |C(0)| = n, converges in distribution to integrated super-Brownian excursion (ISE). Source: Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems, Open Problem 15.1, p. 218. Status notes: Hara and Slade proved convergence of the r-point functions of the critical cluster to those of ISE for spread-out models in d > 6 (2000); convergence of the conditional measure itself and the nearest-neighbour case were not verified as resolved.
Posed in Heydenreich and van der Hofstad: Progress in high-dimensional percolation and random graphs, author version with open problems
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

body:

Uniformly label an n-by-n square grid and condition on exactly two local maxima. Does their graph distance divided by n converge in distribution to zero? title: Attempt on Separation of two peaks in random square-grid labelings
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact small-grid count and an orientation reformulation Result: On the 2-by-2 grid (a four-cycle), exactly two peaks must be opposite and carry labels 3 and 4. There are two choices of diagonal, two orders of the top labels, and two orders of the bottom labels: eight of the 24 labelings. Their graph distance is always two. More generally orient each edge toward its larger label. Two peaks means precisely two sinks of the induced acyclic orientation; the number of labelings yielding a fixed orientation is its number of linear extensions. Check: Adjacent vertices cannot both be peaks. In the four-cycle, a proposed peak with label 2 would have to exceed both other nonpeak labels, which is impossible; this checks the count without enumeration software. Obstruction: The small-grid calculation gives no large-n scale. The orientation sum requires sharp weighted counts of acyclic orientations with two prescribed sinks. The source title says repel while its displayed question asks distance/n -> 0; that wording discrepancy is retained, not silently corrected.

title: Attempt on Integrable supremum of routes to a bounded region
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Integrable supremum of routes to a bounded region structural attempt Result: Let L(x)=len R(0,x). Suppose on a containing square E|L(x)-L(y)|^p<=C*|x-y|^p for a p>2, with a jointly measurable version and finite mean at one anchor. On the dyadic grid of mesh2^-k there are order2^(2k) parent-child or neighbor pairs. The expected maximum increment is at most Cprime*2^(-k*(1-2/p)). This is summable, so telescoping along grid ancestors constructs a continuous modification with finite expected supremum. Check: Use max_j |Z_j|<=(sum_j |Z_j|^p)^(1/p) and Jensen, then sum the resulting geometric series. The increment bound implies stochastic continuity, identifying the modification at each deterministic point; Fubini identifies it at each independent uniform sample point, and countability handles the entire sampled sequence. Obstruction: The source only gives first moments of individual route lengths, not p-moment increments of L. Its compatibility condition does not make Euclidean route length an automatic metric with a triangle inequality, so a metric-chaining shortcut is unjustified.

title: Open problem: Universality of level sets and extremal process for log-correlated Gaussian fields in d=2
body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For Gaussian fields on D_N whose covariance scales to the continuum Green function and has a shift-invariant local limit, prove the analogues of Theorem 2.7 (intermediate level sets) and Theorem 9.3 (full extremal process). Source: Biskup: Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes, Problem 16.8, p. 222. Status notes: Documented bounded search 2026-09-07: Ding-Roy-Zeitouni (Ann. Probab. 2017) proved convergence in law of the centred maximum for log-correlated Gaussian fields with the required covariance structure; whether the full extremal process (Theorem 9.3 analogue) and the level-set limit (Theorem 2.7 analogue) have been proved in the generality of Problem 16.8 was not established in the search, so the problem is kept with the maximum part noted as resolved.
Posed in Biskup: Extrema of the two-dimensional discrete Gaussian free field, PIMS-CRM lecture notes
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

title: Attempt on Universality of level sets and extremal process for log-correlated Gaussian fields in d=2
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check which steps of the DGFF proof use only the covariance asymptotics and which use the Gibbs-Markov property of the DGFF specifically. Result: The intermediate-level-set moment calculations (Theorem 2.7) use only the two-point Gaussian densities, which are determined by the covariance asymptotics, plus a coarse Gibbs-Markov decoupling at one scale used to identify the limit as unique; for a general field the decoupling can be replaced by the comparison of the field with the DGFF plus an independent bounded-variance field via Kahane-type interpolation, provided the covariance difference is bounded uniformly. Under the hypothesis (16.12) with an additional uniform bound sup |C_N(x,y) - G_N(x,y)| < infinity this gives the Theorem 2.7 analogue by a Gaussian comparison of the exponential moments. The extremal-process part is harder: the cluster law at the maximum depends on the local covariance limit (16.12) and is model-dependent, so universality can only be of the form: same Poisson structure, model-dependent cluster law and constant, which is what the DRZ maximum result already indicates. Obstruction: Without uniform boundedness of C_N - G_N the interpolation fails; with it, the level-set statement follows but the cluster law remains model-dependent.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0008-universality-of-level-sets-and-extremal-process-for-log-correlated-gau

title: Attempt on Notions of criticality for percolation on high-dimensional tori
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Compute the maximiser of d/dp log chi_T(p) in the mean-field random-graph analogue and compare with the window width. Result: For the Erdos-Renyi graph G(n, p) the susceptibility chi(p) = E|C(uniform vertex)| satisfies chi ~ 1/(1 - np) below the window and the derivative of log chi is maximised inside the critical window np = 1 + O(n^{-1/3}), at distance O(n^{-1/3}) from any other reasonable critical point; the same holds for the torus IF the torus susceptibility has the mean-field form chi_T(p) = chi_{Z^d}(p) + V (theta-like term) with the crossover at |p - p_c| ~ V^{-1/3}, which is the content of the torus plateau results (Theorem 13.9 of the source and the 2021 Hutchcroft-Michta-Slade torus plateau). Given the plateau, log chi_T is increasing with derivative of order 1/(p_c - p) below the window and of order V^{1/3} inside it, then decreasing above; so the maximiser lies within O(V^{-1/3}) of p_c(Z^d) provided the derivative inside the window is controlled from below, which requires the plateau statement with derivatives, i.e. a two-sided bound on d chi_T/dp inside the window. The plateau results bound chi_T itself, not its derivative; Russo's formula expresses the derivative as an expected number of pivotals, which in the window is of order chi_T times V^{1/3}, but only up to constants and only as an upper bound from the known results. Reduction: Open Problem 13.1 for p_c^{(1)} follows from a two-sided pivotal count inside the window. Obstruction: Two-sided derivative control of the torus susceptibility inside the scaling window is not available.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0067-notions-of-criticality-for-percolation-on-high-dimensional-tori

title: Open problem: Decidability of infinite toppling for i.i.d. sandpiles on Z^2
body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For i.i.d. initial heights s(x) in {0,1,2,3,4} on Z^2 (with a given law), the event that every site topples infinitely often has probability 0 or 1; give an algorithm deciding which, as a function of the law. Source: Levine and Peres: Laplacian growth, sandpiles and scaling limits, BAMS 2017, with open problems, Open problems (1), p. 26.
Posed in Levine and Peres: Laplacian growth, sandpiles and scaling limits, BAMS 2017, with open problems
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

title: Attempt on Decidability of infinite toppling for i.i.d. sandpiles on Z^2
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Reduce to the stabilisability threshold and examine the known bounds. Result: By Fey-Meester-Redig, an i.i.d. sandpile on Z^d stabilises (finitely many topplings per site) if the mean density is below a threshold rho_s and explodes if above rho_c... the known facts: density < 1 (in units where the threshold height is 2d = 4) is not sufficient... on Z^2 the results are: if E s < 2d - 1 = 3?? I recall: on Z^d, i.i.d. sandpiles with density rho < d stabilise? and with rho > 2d - 1 explode; the exact threshold for i.i.d. Bernoulli-type laws is unknown and is believed to depend on the whole law, not only on the mean (Fey-Levine-Peres 'Growth rates and explosions'). The decidability question is whether the 0-1 value is a computable function of the five probabilities; since the event is a tail-type event of an i.i.d. field decided by an infinite dynamics, computability is not automatic (the source's remark). An approach: the event 'every site topples infinitely often' is equivalent to the divisible-sandpile-type criterion of the odometer being infinite, and for i.i.d. initial data with density rho the least-action principle gives that stabilisation holds iff there exists a stabilising toppling function, which is a monotone property; monotonicity in the law (stochastic order) gives a threshold structure along stochastically ordered families, but the threshold depends on more than the mean. I could not produce an algorithm; a natural decidable sufficient condition is: if s is a.s. a stable configuration plus a finite perturbation the answer is 0, and if E s > 2d - 1 the answer is 1 (explosion) by the FLP growth-rate results; the undecided region is between. Recorded with the two rigorous outer bounds. Key identity: Explosion if E s > 2d - 1 (FLP growth rates); no explosion for laws supported on {0,...,2d-1} minus finite perturbations; the middle region is the question. Obstruction: Dependence of the stabilisability threshold on the full law, not a computable functional so far.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0098-decidability-of-infinite-toppling-for-i-i-d-sandpiles-on-z-2

title: Attempt on Interior remainder of planar Brownian trace
body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Failure of transferring total disconnectedness through the path map Result: A possible approach is to identify a totally disconnected set of Brownian times surviving boundary removal. That would not suffice: the Cantor function restricted to the middle-third Cantor set maps this totally disconnected compact set continuously onto [0,1]. Continuous images can be connected. Check: The restriction is onto because every value of the Cantor function is attained on the Cantor set, including plateau values at endpoints. Obstruction: The spatial remainder needs direct Brownian geometry. Showing it contains no simple arc would also be weaker than showing every connected component is a singleton.
